s: Adonijah tries to seize the throne, but David has Solomon anointed king.
David's last charge to Solomon, and his death. Solomon secures his throne.
Solomon asks God for wisdom, not riches, and judges wisely between two mothers.
Solomon's officials and his great wisdom and prosperity.
Solomon makes an agreement with Hiram of Tyre for cedar and craftsmen to build the temple.
Solomon builds the temple.
Solomon builds his palace, and Hiram makes the bronze works of the temple.
The ark is brought into the temple and the cloud of glory fills it. Solomon prays at the dedication.
God appears to Solomon again, with a promise and a warning.
The queen of Sheba visits and marvels at Solomon's wisdom and wealth.
Solomon's many foreign wives turn his heart to other gods. God promises to tear away most of the kingdom.
The kingdom splits in two: Rehoboam rules Judah, and Jeroboam rules Israel and sets up golden calves.
A man of God from Judah prophesies against Jeroboam's altar.
Jeroboam's son dies as the prophet foretold. Rehoboam's reign in Judah.
Kings of Judah and Israel. Asa reforms Judah.
More kings of Israel, ending with Ahab, who serves Baal.
Elijah announces a drought. He is fed by ravens and raises the widow of Zarephath's son.
Elijah defeats the prophets of Baal on Mount Carmel, and fire falls from heaven. The rain returns.
Elijah flees Jezebel to Mount Horeb and hears God in a still small voice. He calls Elisha.
Ahab defeats the Syrians but spares their king.
Jezebel has Naboth killed so Ahab can take his vineyard. Elijah pronounces judgment, and Ahab humbles himself.
The prophet Micaiah foretells defeat. Ahab dies in battle at Ramoth-gilead.

3: Solomon asks not for riches or power but for wisdom to rule justly, and God is pleased.
8: Solomon's temple is finished and God's glory fills it. For centuries it will be the centre of Israel's worship.
12: After Solomon's death the ten northern tribes break away. From now on there are two kingdoms, Israel in the north and Judah in the south.
18: Elijah challenges the prophets of Baal, and God answers with fire. The people cry out: the Lord, he is God.
19: Elijah finds God not in the wind, earthquake or fire, but in a gentle whisper.
